stem:
The diagram shows lines $AB$ and $CD$ meeting at $O$. A right-angle mark sits at $O$, and all four angles at $O$ are equal.

What can Arnav conclude?

options.text: Each angle is a right angle, and that label alone is the full conclusion.
The lines are perpendicular even when they stay apart and never meet.
The lines are perpendicular, because four equal angles at an intersection are each $90^{\circ}$.
The lines are perpendicular because the printed word equal is the standout word.

teacher.key_rationale: Four equal angles at a meeting sum to 360°, so each is 90° and the lines are perpendicular. Stopping at the right-angle label, dropping the meeting condition, or grabbing the word equal alone all miss that test.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle rods as intersecting lines AB and CD at O with a right-angle mark.
